### Run OpenCode

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/index.mdx

Start OpenCode from within your project directory.

```bash
opencode
```

--------------------------------

### Start the SolidStart development server with npm run dev

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/README.md

After installing dependencies with npm install (or pnpm install or yarn), run npm run dev to start the development server. Add -- --open to open the app in a new browser tab.

```bash
npm run dev

# or start the server and open the app in a new browser tab
npm run dev -- --open
```

### Initialize Project with /init

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/index.mdx

```bash
/init
```

--------------------------------

### Run startup benchmark with strobe

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/desktop/README.md

Use these commands to benchmark desktop startup performance with strobe. The first command compares two packaged builds or installed channels for a returning user; the second measures the first launch after an install; the third measures the dev loop's cold start. Packaged builds must be created with OPENCODE_CHANNEL=beta or prod.

```bash
# A returning user's launches of two packaged builds (pack each with OPENCODE_CHANNEL=beta or prod), or two installed
# channels.
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target desktop --base exe:<old>/OpenCode.exe --head exe:<new>/OpenCode.exe
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target desktop --base app:opencode --head app:opencode-beta

# The first launch after an install.
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target install --base app:opencode --head app:opencode-beta

# The dev loop's cold start, dev against this checkout.
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target dev --base origin/dev --head .
```

From this screen, the user can undelete a note or permanently delete it.

### Window setup with createKeyed and cleanup function

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Window setup must be synchronous; start asynchronous work inside createKeyed or createLatest. Registrations made through ctx are withdrawn when the owning scope ends. Return a cleanup function for other resources like timers.

```tsx
import { Command, createKeyed, Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { Changes } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/review"

export default Plugin.define({
  i18n: { en: { changes: "Show changes" } },
  setup(ctx) {
    // Runs once per active generation of Changes; the command is withdrawn with it.
    createKeyed(ctx.use(Changes), (changes) => {
      ctx.add(Command, () => ({
        id: "changes",
        title: ctx.t("changes"),
        run: () => {
          const session = ctx.sessions.current()

          if (session) changes.open(session)
        },
      }))
    })

    const timer = setInterval(() => console.log("still here"), 60_000)

    return () => clearInterval(timer)
  },
})
```

### Find instances with SelectorOptions examples

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-code-connect/references/api.md

Usage examples for finding instances by specific hierarchy path or traversing all nested instances.

```javascript
// Find icon only in specific hierarchy
const icon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  path: ['Header', 'Actions', 'IconSlot']
})

// Search everywhere including nested instances
const anyIcon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  traverseInstances: true
})
```

import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export const main: Plugin.MainSetup = (ctx) => {
  ctx.log.write("info", "acme started")
}

### Return a cleanup function from setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

Return a cleanup function to release resources owned by the plugin. The example subscribes to `session.execution.succeeded` and stops the subscription when cleanup runs.

```ts
setup(context) {
  const stop = context.data.on("session.execution.succeeded", () => {})
  return () => stop()
}
```

### Return a cleanup function from setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

`setup` may return a cleanup function that runs when the plugin unloads. The context exposes `ctx.app.version`.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  setup(ctx) {
    console.log(`loaded in OpenCode ${ctx.app.version}`)
    return () => console.log("unloaded")
  },
})
```

### Install OpenCode via curl, npm, Homebrew, pacman, paru, mise, or Nix

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/README.md

Installation commands for OpenCode across various package managers and platforms. Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

```bash
# YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash

# Package managers
npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest      # or bun/pnpm/yarn
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2 # macOS and Linux (recommended, always up to date)
brew install opencode              # macOS and Linux (official brew formula, updated less)
sudo pacman -S opencode            # Arch Linux (Stable)
paru -S opencode-beta              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
mise use -g opencode               # Any OS
nix run github:anomalyco/opencode  # Nix
```

### Type a window setup with Plugin.Setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Window setup in src/gui/window.tsx typed as Plugin.Setup<typeof definition>, which types ctx.stores from the declared stores. Provides the Notes token from the contract.

```tsx
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { Notes } from "./contract"
import type { definition } from "./definition"

export const setup: Plugin.Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  ctx.provide(Notes, { count: () => ctx.stores.notes.value.count })
}
```

--------------------------------

### Initial load and background plugin boot flow

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/specs/v2/catalog-config-plugin-lifecycle.md

Illustrates building a baseline catalog from immediate sources while background fibers activate slower plugins asynchronously.

```ts
LocationServiceMap.get(ref)
  → build location layer
    → Catalog.layer creates empty catalog state
    → PluginBoot.layer activates immediately available plugins
      → ConfigProviderPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → ModelsDevPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → AuthPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
    → Catalog.layer applies active transforms during boot
    → apply policy
    → materialize baseline provider/model catalog
  → PluginBoot baseline ready
    → Frontend.fetchCatalog()

PluginBoot background fiber
  → install/update plugin packages concurrently
  → activate completed plugins
    → Catalog.transform()
      → transform(updateCatalog)
        → Catalog internally rebuilds
          → Catalog.Event.Updated
            → Frontend.refetchCatalog()
```

--------------------------------

### Create a GUI main plugin setup with pairing service and screen blocker

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-plugins/README.md

Defines a `Plugin.MainSetup` that wires a pairing state machine to CLI service commands, power-save blocking, and persisted settings. Register it as the default export; it provides the `Pairing` service and cleans up on disposal.

```ts
import { execFile } from "node:child_process"
import { powerSaveBlocker } from "electron"
import { Schema } from "effect"
import { builtinMainContext } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/builtin"
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/main"
import { Pairing } from "./contract"
import { createDispatch } from "./dispatch"
import {
  createPairingMainState,
  pairingMainEffectFailed,
  selectBlocker,
  transitionPairingMain,
  type PairingMainEffect,
  type ServiceRequest,
} from "./main-machine"

type Waiter = { resolve: (value: boolean | undefined) => void; reject: (error: Error) => void }

const setup: Plugin.MainSetup = (ctx) => {
  // Whether main keeps the display awake; stored before in the desktop's own settings namespace.
  const stored = builtinMainContext(ctx).storage.store("keepScreenActive", {
    schema: Schema.Boolean,
    initial: false,
    from: { state: ["opencode.settings", "keepScreenActive"] },
  })

  const cli = ctx.cli
  const log = ctx.log
  const current = { state: createPairingMainState(), waiter: 0 }
  // Each running command's abort controller, and each caller waiting on a command.
  const commands = new Map<number, AbortController>()
  const waiters = new Map<number, Waiter>()

  const dispatch = createDispatch({
    read: () => current.state,
    write: (state) => {
      current.state = state
    },
    transition: transitionPairingMain,
    run: (effect: PairingMainEffect) => run(effect),
    failed: pairingMainEffectFailed,
  })

  // The OS can drop the blocker, so whether main holds it is asked each time.
  const screenActive = () => {
    const id = selectBlocker(current.state)

    return id !== undefined && powerSaveBlocker.isStarted(id)
  }

  const run = (effect: PairingMainEffect) => {
    if (effect.type === "blocker.start")
      return dispatch({ type: "blocker.started", id: powerSaveBlocker.start("prevent-display-sleep") })

    if (effect.type === "blocker.stop") {
      if (powerSaveBlocker.isStarted(effect.id)) powerSaveBlocker.stop(effect.id)

      return
    }

    if (effect.type === "persist.screen") return stored.set(effect.enabled)

    if (effect.type === "service.abort") {
      commands.get(effect.attempt)?.abort()
      commands.delete(effect.attempt)

      return
    }

    if (effect.type === "waiter.resolve" || effect.type === "waiter.reject") {
      const waiter = waiters.get(effect.waiter)

      waiters.delete(effect.waiter)

      if (effect.type === "waiter.resolve") return waiter?.resolve(effect.value)

      return waiter?.reject(new Error(effect.message))
    }

    // Remote access is a setting of the background service, so it changes through the CLI the app runs, as with
    // `opencode pair --remote`. A hung command ends at its timeout, so the next one always runs.
    const attempt = effect.attempt
    const controller = new AbortController()

    commands.set(attempt, controller)
    execFile(
      cli.command[0] ?? "opencode",
      [...cli.command.slice(1), "service", ...effect.args],
      { signal: AbortSignal.any([ctx.signal, controller.signal]), timeout: effect.timeoutMs, windowsHide: true },
      (error, stdout, stderr) => {
        commands.delete(attempt)

        if (!error) return dispatch({ type: "service.succeeded", attempt, stdout: stdout.trim() })
        log.write("error", "pairing service command failed", { args: effect.args, error: error.message, stderr })
        dispatch({ type: "service.failed", attempt, message: error.message })
      },
    )
  }

  // Queues a command. A read stops when its caller goes away; a change goes on.
  const service = (request: ServiceRequest, signal?: AbortSignal) => {
    current.waiter += 1
    const waiter = current.waiter
    const cancel = () => dispatch({ type: "waiter.cancelled", waiter })

    return new Promise<boolean | undefined>((resolve, reject) => {
      waiters.set(waiter, { resolve, reject })
      signal?.addEventListener("abort", cancel, { once: true })
      dispatch({ type: "service.requested", waiter, request })

      if (signal?.aborted) cancel()
    }).finally(() => signal?.removeEventListener("abort", cancel))
  }

  if (stored.value) dispatch({ type: "screen.set", enabled: true, started: false })
  ctx.onCleanup(() => dispatch({ type: "disposed" }))

  ctx.provide(Pairing, {
    remote: async (_, caller) => (await service({ kind: "get-remote" }, caller.signal)) === true,
    // Changing the setting stops the service, and starting it again brings it back. A window that closes meanwhile
    // does not cancel the change.
    setRemote: async (enabled) => {
      await service({ kind: "set-remote", enabled })
    },
    screenActive,
    setScreenActive: (enabled) => dispatch({ type: "screen.set", enabled, started: screenActive() }),
  })
}

export default setup

```

--------------------------------

### Combine definition, setup, and main in src/gui.tsx

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Entry file that imports the definition, window setup, and main setup and exports the combined plugin via Plugin.define.

```tsx
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { definition } from "./gui/definition"
import { main } from "./gui/main"
import { setup } from "./gui/window"

export default Plugin.define({ ...definition, setup, main })
```

### Example playground session

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/process-daemon/README.md

Sample sequence exercising demo, terminal creation, shell commands, screen/replay inspection, resize, kill, and quit.

```text
demo
new
run printf '\033[32mgreen from the shell\033[0m\n'
new /bin/sh
list
use 1
screen
replay 1 0
resize 72 20
kill 2
quit
```

### Install OpenCode CLI

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/index.mdx

Install the OpenCode CLI using one of several package managers or installers. The npm package uses a postinstall script to select the native binary; Bun and pnpm require explicit script permission, Vite+ needs no flag, and mise requires version 2026.10.9 or later. Windows package managers are not supported.

```shell
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

```shell
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
```

```shell
npm install -g @opencode/cli
```

```shell
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
```

```shell
pnpm add -g --allow-build=@opencode/cli @opencode/cli
```

```shell
yarn global add @opencode/cli
```

```shell
vp install -g @opencode/cli
```

```shell
paru -S opencode-beta
```

```shell
mise use -g opencode
```

Install the plugin globally to automatically log each OpenCode conversation as a session in Helicone.

```bash
npm install -g opencode-helicone-session
```

### Register a Server with ready and entries

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Use ctx.add to register a Server that contributes a list of server connections. Startup waits for every source to be ready; a ready source's entries are its complete inventory. Each entry's key is <plugin id>:<id>.

```ts
import { Server } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

ctx.add(
  Server,
  (): Server => ({
    ready: loaded(),
    entries: machines().map((machine) => ({
      id: machine.id,
      name: machine.name,
      label: "Acme",
      state: machine.url ? "ready" : "starting",
      http: machine.url ? { url: machine.url } : undefined,
    })),
  }),
)
```

Crée le dossier .opencode/themes à la racine du projet et initialise un fichier de thème local.

```bash
mkdir -p .opencode/themes

```

### Define a GUI plugin with Plugin.define and setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

A plugin's setup runs in every desktop app window. Pass it to Plugin.define from @opencode/plugin/gui in the plugin's ./gui-experimental file. setup is synchronous and may return a cleanup function.

```tsx
import { Command, Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export default Plugin.define({
  i18n: { en: { open: "Open Acme" } },
  setup(ctx) {
    ctx.add(Command, () => ({
      id: "open",
      title: ctx.t("open"),
      run: () => ctx.system.openExternal("https://acme.example"),
    }))
  },
})
```

### Install the GitHub agent in your repository

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx

Install the GitHub agent in your repository. This sets up the necessary GitHub Actions workflow and guides you through the configuration process.

```bash
opencode github install
```

### Plugin setup with ctx.use, ctx.stores, and ctx.add

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-plugins/README.md

Access another plugin's contract via ctx.use(Changes) and read a declared store with ctx.stores.prefs.value, which is loaded before setup. Contribute a command using the function form so labels are re-read when the language changes.

```ts
const setup: Plugin.Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  const changes = ctx.use(Changes) // Accessor<Live<Changes>>
  const prefs = ctx.stores.prefs.value // loaded before setup
  ctx.add(Command, () => ({ id: "open", title: ctx.t("open"), run: () => ctx.layout.settings(ctx.id) }))
}
```

### Install xvfb and start virtual display for headless Linux copy/paste

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/troubleshooting.mdx

Install xvfb and run a virtual display for copy/paste in headless environments. The export sets DISPLAY to the virtual display.

```bash
apt install -y xvfb
# and run:
Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1024x768x24 > /dev/null 2>&1 &
export DISPLAY=:99.0
```

```

### TextNode Range Methods

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-figjam/references/edit-text.md

SDK methods on TextNode for getting and setting properties across a specific character range (start to end indices).

```APIDOC
## TextNode Range Methods

### Description
Methods available on `TextNode` instances to apply mixed styling, fonts, fills, hyperlinks, and list options to specific character ranges.

### Methods
- `textNode.setRangeFontName(start, end, fontName)`
- `textNode.setRangeFontSize(start, end, size)`
- `textNode.setRangeFills(start, end, fills)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextDecoration(start, end, decoration)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextCase(start, end, textCase)`
- `textNode.setRangeLetterSpacing(start, end, spacing)`
- `textNode.setRangeLineHeight(start, end, lineHeight)`
- `textNode.setRangeHyperlink(start, end, hyperlink)`
- `textNode.setRangeListOptions(start, end, listOptions)`
- `textNode.setRangeIndentation(start, end, indentation)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontName(start, end)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontSize(start, end)`

### Usage Examples
```javascript
// Make "Hello" bold (characters 0-5)
textNode.setRangeFontName(0, 5, { family: 'Inter', style: 'Bold' });

// Make "World" red (characters 6-11)
textNode.setRangeFills(6, 11, [{ type: 'SOLID', color: { r: 1, g: 0, b: 0 } }]);

// Change size of "World"
textNode.setRangeFontSize(6, 11, 24);

// Get properties for a range
const fontAtStart = textNode.getRangeFontName(0, 1);
const sizeAtEnd = textNode.getRangeFontSize(10, 11);
```
```

### Main setup with async and ctx.onCleanup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

main may be async. Return or resolve to a cleanup function for resources it opens, or register it with ctx.onCleanup(fn). ctx.onCleanup runs functions when the plugin is disabled, reloaded, or removed, or the app quits, last registered first.

```ts
async main(ctx) {
  const socket = await connect(ctx.options)

  ctx.onCleanup(() => socket.close())
}
```

### Add a custom LSP server with command and extensions

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/lsp.mdx

Add custom LSP servers by specifying the command and file extensions. The example defines a server named `custom-lsp`.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "lsp": {
    "custom-lsp": {
      "command": ["custom-lsp-server", "--stdio"],
      "extensions": [".custom"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Generate Video with Google Veo and Runway

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/ai/README.md

Use the experimental Video API to generate videos. The first example submits a generation and waits for the result, materializing the video asset before persisting. The second example starts a generation, saves the token, and resumes it later. The third example streams generation events. All providers are asynchronous and use a submit-then-poll pattern.

```typescript
import { Video } from "@opencode/ai/experimental"
import { Google, Runway } from "@opencode/ai/providers"

const google = Google.configure({ apiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY })

// Simple: submit and wait.
const program = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const response = yield* Video.generate(
    {
      model: google.video("veo-3.1-generate-preview"),
      prompt: "Panning wide shot of a calico kitten sleeping in the sunshine",
      aspect: "16:9",
      resolution: "1080p",
      durationSeconds: 8,
      providerOptions: { personGeneration: "allow_adult" },
    },
    { poll: { interval: "10 seconds", timeout: "10 minutes" } },
  )
  // Veo serves files for two days behind the API key. The asset knows the deadline (`expiresAt`) and carries the
  // download credentials only on the live instance (`asset.headers`), never in `source` or JSON: materialize
  // before persisting, or the persisted URL cannot be fetched again.
  return yield* response.video.materialize()
})

// Explicit control: keep the handle, persist the token, resume elsewhere.
const controlled = Effect.gen(function* () {
  const generation = yield* Video.start({ model: google.video("veo-3.1-generate-preview"), prompt })
  generation.id // provider operation / task / request id
  generation.status // "queued" | "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "expired"
  generation.token // route-owned JSON: `{ operation }`, `{ requestID }`, or `{ taskID }`
  // The token carries no route identity: persist the provider and model ID alongside it, since `resume` needs the model.
  const saved = JSON.stringify(generation.token)

  const resumed = yield* Video.resume(google.video("veo-3.1-generate-preview"), JSON.parse(saved))
  return yield* resumed.await({ poll: { interval: "10 seconds" } })
})

// Progress as a stream: generation-queued | generation-progress | video | finish.
const events = Video.stream({ model: Runway.configure({ apiKey }).video("gen4.5"), prompt }, { poll })
```

### Define GUI plugin with setup and main in src/gui.tsx

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Each process evaluates the whole ./gui-experimental file and reads its default export. Windows run setup; the desktop app's main process runs main. Because both processes evaluate the same file, each stands in inert placeholders for the other process's modules, so keep each process's code inside its own setup.

```tsx
import { shell } from "electron"
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export default Plugin.define({
  setup(ctx) {
    // Window code: Solid components, ctx.layout, ctx.add(Command, …).
  },
  main(ctx) {
    // Main code: electron, Node built-ins, ctx.windows.
    ctx.windows.on("open", () => shell.beep())
  },
})
```

```ts
const created = await ctx.session.create({ title: "Review" })
const session = await ctx.session.get({ sessionID })
const messages = await ctx.session.context({ sessionID })
```

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "lsp": {
    "rust": {
      "command": ["rust-analyzer"],
      "env": {
        "RUST_LOG": "debug"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Write the window entry with lazy-loaded settings page and Pairing

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-plugins/README.md

Defines the plugin setup for the desktop window, returning early when `ctx.desktop` is absent. The settings page loads behind `lazy()` and preloads on idle; the local server is found via `ctx.servers` by `builtin`, and remote access/display entries appear only while pairing status is `active`.

```tsx
import { lazy, onCleanup, Suspense } from "solid-js"
import { Command, SettingsPage, type Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { onIdle } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/builtin"
import { Pairing } from "./contract"
import type definition from "./index"

const setup: Plugin.Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.desktop) return
  const layout = ctx.layout
  const servers = ctx.servers
  const pairing = ctx.use(Pairing)
  const Page = lazy(() => import("./page"))
  // Settings rows are small; load them while idle so settings opens without a blank row.
  onCleanup(onIdle(() => void Page.preload()))

  // The desktop's own server. Its ref is already authenticated in this window, so codes need no main process.
  const local = () =>
    servers
      .list()
      .map((id) => servers.get(id))
      .find((server) => server?.builtin)

  ctx.add(SettingsPage, {
    id: "pairing",
    icon: "outline-pair",
    get title() {
      return ctx.t("title")
    },
    get entries() {
      const pairingEntry = { id: "pairing", title: ctx.t("title"), keywords: "pair device qr phone remote" }

      // Remote access and the display setting exist only while pairing's main side answers.
      if (pairing().status !== "active") return [pairingEntry]

      return [
        pairingEntry,
        {
          id: "settings-remote-access",
          title: ctx.t("remote.title"),
          description: ctx.t("remote.description"),
          keywords: "internet tunnel opentunnel",
        },
        {
          id: "settings-keep-screen-active",
          title: ctx.t("screenActive.title"),
          description: ctx.t("screenActive.description"),
          keywords: "display sleep awake local",
        },
      ]
    },
    render: () => (
      <Suspense>
        <Page server={local} pairing={pairing} />
      </Suspense>
    ),
  })

  ctx.add(Command, () => ({
    id: "open",
    title: ctx.t("command.title"),
    group: ctx.t("command.category.server"),
    run: () => layout.settings("pairing"),
  }))
}

export default setup
```

### desktop.launch(path: string, app?: string): Promise<void>

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Opens a path with an app, or with the default app. Desktop only.

```APIDOC
## desktop.launch(path: string, app?: string): Promise<void>

### Description
Opens a path with an app, or with the default app. Desktop only.

### Method
desktop.launch

### Parameters
- **path** (string) - Required - The path to open.
- **app** (string) - Optional - The app to use. If omitted, the default app is used.

### Response
Returns a Promise that resolves when the launch is complete.
```

### Define project instructions in AGENTS.md

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/ar/rules.mdx

An example AGENTS.md file configuring project structure, code standards, and monorepo conventions for an SST v3 project.

```markdown
# SST v3 Monorepo Project

This is an SST v3 monorepo with TypeScript. The project uses bun workspaces for package management.

## Project Structure

- `packages/` - Contains all workspace packages (functions, core, web, etc.)
- `infra/` - Infrastructure definitions split by service (storage.ts, api.ts, web.ts)
- `sst.config.ts` - Main SST configuration with dynamic imports

## Code Standards

- Use TypeScript with strict mode enabled
- Shared code goes in `packages/core/` with proper exports configuration
- Functions go in `packages/functions/`
- Infrastructure should be split into logical files in `infra/`

## Monorepo Conventions

- Import shared modules using workspace names: `@my-app/core/example`
```

### SetupContext and Context interface reference

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

TypeScript interface definitions for SetupContext and Context, listing the properties and methods available on the GUI plugin host context.

```ts
interface SetupContext<D> extends Context {
  stores: Record<string, Persisted<unknown> | ((session: SessionRef) => Persisted<unknown>)>
}

interface Context {
  id: string
  options: PluginOptions
  client: OpenCodeClient
  app: App
  signal: AbortSignal
  add<T>(registry: Registry<T>, item: () => T | undefined): Cleanup
  add<T>(registry: Registry<T>, item: T): Cleanup
  list<T>(registry: Registry<T>): T[]
  provide<T>(token: Contract<T>, impl: T): Cleanup
  use<T>(token: Contract<T>): () => Live<T>
  use<S extends IpcSpec>(token: Ipc<S>): () => Live<IpcClient<S>>
  main<S extends IpcSpec>(token: Ipc<S>): IpcClient<S>
  t(key: string, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): string
  plural(key: string, count: number, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): string
  layout: Layout
  sessions: Sessions
  screen: Screen
  servers: Servers
  storage: Storage
  dialogs: Dialogs
  toast: Toasts
  attention: Attention
  tabs: Tabs
  keybinds: Keybinds
  commands: Commands
  links: Links
  embeds: Embeds
  ui: Ui
  system: System
  desktop: Desktop | undefined
  locale: Locale
  appearance: Appearance
  router: Router
  workspaces: Workspaces
}
```

### Import a main store from the desktop settings file with builtinMainContext

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-plugins/README.md

Creates a main store for saved SSH hosts, importing the older `ssh.servers` key from the desktop settings file via `from: { settings: ... }`. Use `{ state: [namespace, key] }` instead to name a key of another main storage namespace.

```typescript
// The saved hosts; stored before in the desktop settings file.
const saved = builtinMainContext(ctx).storage.store("servers", {
  schema: Schema.Array(SshConfig),
  initial: [],
  from: { settings: "ssh.servers" },
})
```

### Run GitHub snapshot script with GITHUB_TOKEN

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/README.md

The snapshot script uses GITHUB_TOKEN when it is set; CI passes the workflow's own token. Never commit a token.

```bash
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) bun ./script/github-snapshot.ts
```

### Configure Atomic Chat local provider in opencode.json

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx

Use this to connect opencode to a local Atomic Chat server via an OpenAI-compatible API. The baseURL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1; adjust host and port to match your setup. Model IDs must match those returned by GET /v1/models.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "atomic-chat": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Atomic Chat (local)",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "<your-model-id>": {
          "name": "<your-model-name>"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Define a Contract with a valid and invalid token id

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Use `Contract.define` to create a token. A plugin can only provide tokens whose id is its own id or starts with it, as `<id>.<name>`. The second example uses the id `"badge"`, which would cause `ctx.provide` to throw in plugin `acme`.

```ts
Contract.define<AcmeBadge, "acme.badge">("acme.badge") // Plugin acme can provide it.
Contract.define<AcmeBadge, "badge">("badge") // ctx.provide throws in plugin acme.
```

### Run backend and app dev servers separately for local UI changes

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/app/AGENTS.md

`opencode dev web` proxies the hosted app, so local UI/CSS changes won't appear there. Start the backend from the repository root and the app from packages/app, then open http://localhost:4444, which targets the backend at http://localhost:4096.

```shell
bun dev serve --port 4096
```

```shell
bun dev -- --port 4444
```

### Run OpenCode from WSL in a Windows project path

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/windows-wsl.mdx

Navigates to a Windows drive mount path under /mnt/ and launches OpenCode.

```bash
cd /mnt/c/Users/YourName/project
opencode
```

--------------------------------

### GET /session/:id

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx

Get session details by ID. Returns the Session object.

```APIDOC
## GET /session/:id

### Description
Get session details.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/session/:id

### Parameters
#### Path Parameters
- **id** (string) - Required - Session ID

### Response
#### Success Response (200)
- **Session** - The Session object
```

### Quick Start: Define a Tool and Execute Code with CodeMode

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/codemode/README.md

Create a tool with Tool.make, wrap it in a CodeMode runtime, and execute a program that calls the tool. The result is always a CodeMode.Result.

```typescript
import { CodeMode, Namespace, Tool } from "@opencode/codemode"
import { Effect, Schema } from "effect"

const lookupOrder = Tool.make({
  description: "Look up an order by ID",
  input: Schema.Struct({ id: Schema.String }),
  output: Schema.Struct({ id: Schema.String, status: Schema.String }),
  execute: ({ id }) => Effect.succeed({ id, status: "open" }),
})

const runtime = CodeMode.make({
  tools: { orders: { lookup: lookupOrder } },
})

const result = await Effect.runPromise(
  runtime.execute(`
    const order = await tools.orders.lookup({ id: "order_42" })
    return { id: order.id, needsAttention: order.status !== "complete" }
  `),
)
```

### Stop and start the service explicitly

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/troubleshooting.mdx

Explicitly stops then starts the background service. Service commands are only needed when diagnosing its lifecycle, since OpenCode normally discovers or starts the service automatically.

```bash
opencode service stop
opencode service start
```

### Start opencode mini with a model and initial prompt

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/cli/commands.mdx

Begins a minimal session using the specified model and an initial prompt.

```bash
$ opencode mini --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 --prompt "Summarize this repository"
```

### Automatically review pull requests with OpenCode

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/github.mdx

Use this workflow to automatically review PRs when they are opened or updated. If no `prompt` is provided, OpenCode defaults to reviewing the pull request. `issues: write` lets OpenCode react to and comment on the PR, since GitHub handles PR comments through the issues API. This example is intended for PRs from branches in the same repository; PRs from forks normally get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and no secrets.

```yaml
name: opencode-review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: anomalyco/opencode/github@latest
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
          use_github_token: true
          prompt: |
            Review this pull request:
            - Check for code quality issues
            - Look for potential bugs
            - Suggest improvements
```

### Benchmark session or timeline code with strobe against origin/dev

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/app/AGENTS.md

Run this strobe command before changing session or timeline code to compare performance against origin/dev. Replace the placeholder bench path with the relevant area benchmark file.

```shell
strobe bench packages/app/perf/<area>.bench.ts --base origin/dev --head .
```

--------------------------------

### Define a plugin with Plugin.define and async setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/README.md

Use Plugin.define to register a plugin with an id and async setup. Setup registers hooks imperatively via each domain's hook method, such as ctx.provider.transform.

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  setup: async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.provider.transform((editor) => {
      editor.update("example", (provider) => {
        provider.name = "Example"
      })
    })
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Connect an OpenCode Go subscription

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/providers.mdx

Subscribe in the console, copy your API key, then connect it as **OpenCode Go** and select a model. Usage limits, endpoints, and privacy details are covered in the Go guide.

```text
/connect
# Select OpenCode Go, then paste your API key.
/models
```

### Define complete Q1 launch roadmap Gantt diagram

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/gantt.md

Demonstrates a realistic product-launch roadmap with phases, state tags, task dependencies, and milestone tracking.

```mermaid
gantt
    title Q1 Launch Plan
    dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    section Discovery
    User research   :done, r1, 2026-01-05, 2w
    Synthesis       :done, s1, after r1, 1w
    section Design
    Concepts        :active, d1, after s1, 2w
    Design review   :d2, after d1, 3d
    Hi-fi designs   :d3, after d2, 2w
    section Build
    API scaffolding :b1, after d2, 2w
    UI build        :b2, after d3, 3w
    Integration     :b3, after b2, 1w
    section Launch
    Internal beta   :l1, after b3, 1w
    Fixes           :crit, l2, after l1, 5d
    Ship            :milestone, after l2, 0d
```

### GET /session/:id/todo

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx

Get the todo list for a session. Returns an array of Todo objects.

```APIDOC
## GET /session/:id/todo

### Description
Get the todo list for a session.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/session/:id/todo

### Parameters
#### Path Parameters
- **id** (string) - Required - Session ID

### Response
#### Success Response (200)
- **Todo[]** - Array of Todo objects
```

### View serve subcommands and flags with --help

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/cli/commands.mdx

Lists all subcommands and flags for the serve command.

```bash
$ opencode serve --help
```
